es.summary: Acumulación de líquido intersticial en tejidos periféricos, frecuentemente en miembros inferiores, debido a desequilibrio entre presión hidrostática y oncótica.
key_points: Puede ser signo de insuficiencia cardíaca, renal o hepática.
Se evalúa por inspección, palpación y medición del perímetro.
El tratamiento incluye control de la causa y manejo del exceso de líquido.
Complicaciones incluyen úlceras por presión y desequilibrio electrolítico.

pathophysiology: Aumento de presión hidrostática capilar o disminución de presión oncótica.
Retención de sodio y agua por insuficiencia de órganos o uso de diuréticos.
Obstrucción del retorno venoso o linfático provoca acumulación intersticial.
risk_factors: Uso prolongado de fármacos que retienen sodio (corticoides, AINES).
signs_symptoms: Aumento de volumen en tobillos, pies o manos.
Piel brillante, tensada y con fóvea al presionar (signo de Godet).
Sensación de pesadez o rigidez en la zona afectada.
Disminución de la movilidad articular si el edema es severo.
diagnostics: Inspección y medición del perímetro de extremidades.
Ecografía Doppler para descartar trombosis venosa profunda.
Laboratorio: Na+, K+, creatinina, albúmina, BNP según sospecha.
Radiografía de tórax si se sospecha insuficiencia cardíaca.
treatment: Control de la causa subyacente (ej. terapia de insuficiencia cardíaca).
Restricción de sodio (<2 g/día) y líquidos según indicación.
Diuréticos de asa (furosemida) o tiazídicos según prescripción.
Elevación de extremidades y uso de medias de compresión graduada.
complications: Úlceras por presión y dermatitis por maceración.
Trombosis venosa profunda por estasis sanguínea.
Reducción de la perfusión tisular y compromiso funcional.
nursing_care: Evaluar grado de edema y registrar cambios de perímetro cada 24 h.
Monitorear signos vitales, especialmente presión arterial y frecuencia cardíaca.
Aplicar medidas de elevación y compresión según orden médica.
Controlar ingesta y salida de líquidos; registrar balance hídrico.
Observar piel en busca de irritación, eritema o úlceras.
patient_teaching: Explicar la importancia de limitar el consumo de sal y líquidos.
Enseñar la técnica de auto‑medición del perímetro de piernas.
Instruir sobre el uso correcto de medias de compresión.
Promover actividad física ligera para mejorar retorno venoso.
Alertar sobre signos de alarma: dolor intenso, enrojecimiento o calor.

outcomes: Balance hídrico: mantener ingesta y salida de líquidos equilibradas en 48 h.
Reducción del edema: disminuir 1 grado de edema en 72 h.

interventions.action: Registrar balance hídrico cada 8 h y notificar desviaciones >500 mL.
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar rápidamente acumulación de líquido.

interventions.action: Elevar extremidades por encima del nivel del corazón 30 min, 3 veces al día.
interventions.rationale: Facilita el retorno venoso y reduce la presión capilar.

interventions.action: Aplicar medias de compresión graduada según prescripción.
interventions.rationale: Ayuda a prevenir la estasis y disminuye el edema.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre restricción de sodio (<2 g/día).
interventions.rationale: Disminuye la retención de agua.

interventions.action: Monitorear signos vitales y peso diario.
interventions.rationale: Detecta cambios tempranos en el estado de volumen.

outcomes: Niveles de Na+ y K+ dentro de rangos normales (Na+ 135‑145 mEq/L, K+ 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L) en 48 h.
Sin manifestaciones clínicas de arritmia en 72 h.

interventions.action: Obtener y registrar electrolitos séricos cada 24 h.
interventions.rationale: Permite identificar alteraciones tempranas.

interventions.action: Evaluar estado neurológico y ritmo cardíaco cada turno.
interventions.rationale: Detecta signos de hipopotasemia o hiponatremia.

interventions.action: Administrar suplementos de potasio según orden médica.
interventions.rationale: Previene complicaciones de hipopotasemia.

interventions.action: Enseñar al paciente a reconocer síntomas de desequilibrio electrolítico (palpitaciones, debilidad).
interventions.rationale: Facilita la búsqueda de ayuda oportuna.

interventions.action: Revisar y ajustar la dosis de diuréticos en colaboración con el médico.
interventions.rationale: Evita exceso de pérdida de electrolitos.

en.summary: Accumulation of interstitial fluid in peripheral tissues, most often in the lower extremities, due to an imbalance between hydrostatic and oncotic pressures.
key_points: May be a sign of heart, kidney, or liver failure.
It is assessed by inspection, palpation, and circumference measurement.
Treatment includes addressing the underlying cause and managing excess fluid.
Complications include pressure ulcers and electrolyte imbalance.

pathophysiology: Increased capillary hydrostatic pressure or decreased oncotic pressure.
Sodium and water retention from organ failure or diuretic use.
Venous or lymphatic outflow obstruction leads to interstitial accumulation.
risk_factors: Long‑term use of sodium‑retaining drugs (corticosteroids, NSAIDs).
signs_symptoms: Increased volume in ankles, feet, or hands.
Bright, taut skin with a positive Godet sign when pressed.
Feeling of heaviness or stiffness in the affected area.
Reduced joint mobility if edema is severe.
diagnostics: Inspection and measurement of limb circumference.
Doppler ultrasound to rule out deep venous thrombosis.
Laboratory: Na+, K+, creatinine, albumin, BNP as indicated.
Chest X‑ray if heart failure is suspected.
treatment: Address the underlying cause (e.g., heart failure therapy).
Sodium restriction (<2 g/day) and fluid restriction as indicated.
Loop diuretics (furosemide) or thiazides per prescription.
Elevation of limbs and use of graduated compression stockings.
complications: Reduced tissue perfusion and functional impairment.
nursing_care: Assess the degree of edema and record circumference changes every 24 h.
Monitor vital signs, especially blood pressure and heart rate.
Apply elevation and compression measures as ordered.
Track fluid intake and output; record fluid balance.
Inspect skin for irritation, erythema, or ulcers.
patient_teaching: Explain the importance of limiting salt and fluid intake.
Teach self‑measurement of leg circumference technique.
Instruct on proper use of compression stockings.
Encourage light physical activity to improve venous return.
Alert to warning signs: severe pain, redness, or warmth.

outcomes: Fluid balance: maintain intake and output equilibrium within 48 h.
Edema reduction: decrease edema by 1 grade within 72 h.

interventions.action: Record fluid balance every 8 h and notify deviations >500 mL.
interventions.rationale: Allows rapid detection of fluid accumulation.

interventions.action: Elevate limbs above heart level for 30 min, 3 times daily.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates venous return and reduces capillary pressure.

interventions.action: Apply graduated compression stockings as prescribed.
interventions.rationale: Helps prevent stasis and reduces edema.

interventions.action: Educate the patient on sodium restriction (<2 g/day).
interventions.rationale: Reduces water retention.

interventions.action: Monitor vital signs and daily weight.
interventions.rationale: Detects early changes in volume status.

outcomes: Na+ and K+ levels within normal ranges (Na+ 135‑145 mEq/L, K+ 3.5‑5.0 mEq/L) within 48 h.
No clinical arrhythmia manifestations within 72 h.

interventions.action: Obtain and record serum electrolytes every 24 h.
interventions.rationale: Identifies early alterations.

interventions.action: Assess neurological status and cardiac rhythm each shift.
interventions.rationale: Detects signs of hypokalemia or hyponatremia.

interventions.action: Administer potassium supplements as ordered.
interventions.rationale: Prevents hypokalemia complications.

interventions.action: Teach the patient to recognize symptoms of electrolyte imbalance (palpitations, weakness).
interventions.rationale: Facilitates timely help-seeking.

interventions.action: Review and adjust diuretic dosage in collaboration with the physician.
interventions.rationale: Avoids excessive electrolyte loss.

sources.name: Clinical Nursing Skills: Peripheral Vascular System

key_points.0.quote: Heart failure, liver disease, pregnancy, dietary intake, kidney disease, and some medications all contribute to the onset of edema as well as the severity of the condition.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: However, when there is decreased volume of plasma proteins, or blood pressure is increased significantly, there is a change in net filtration, causing excess fluid buildup in the tissues (edema).

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Whatever the cause, thickening of the arteries increases strain on the heart that can lead to congestive heart failure.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Peripheral edema Swelling of the feet, ankles, legs, hands, and arms

sections.treatment.0.quote: It is important to understand that edema is not a discrete disorder but a sign of an underlying disorder that must be addressed.

sections.treatment.2.quote: She has been given one dose of IV furosemide and reports an improvement in dyspnea.

sections.treatment.3.quote: Elevation of the extremities to promote venous return

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: Elevation of the extremities to promote venous return Muscular activity with gradual comp

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: Document the location and size of any skin ulcers.

sections.patient_teaching.4.quote: Unilateral warmth, redness, tenderness, swelling in the calf, or sudden onset of intense, sharp muscle pain that increases with dorsiflexion of the foot is an indication of a DVT.
